name: EVIL GOODS
description: US direct-to-consumer skincare brand built on beef-tallow and other all-natural formulations (balms, face moisturizers, lip care, magnesium cream) running its own affiliate program: 20% base commission, 60-day cookie, monthly payouts, and lifetime commission on referred customers.

evidence.summary: Evil Goods' own affiliate page (fetched) states a 20% base commission on every sale regardless of volume, rising to 25% at $5,000+ in monthly sales and up to 30% during product launches, with lifetime commission on customers a creator refers and 20% recurring commission on subscription orders for 3 months. It also states a 60-day cookie, monthly payouts with a $50 minimum, a 15% follower discount code, applications reviewed within 48 business hours, and an affiliate contact email (help@evilgoods.com). No statement about an earnings cap appears anywhere on the page, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown, not uncapped.

The same page (fetched) says 'Join 2,500+ affiliates' and claims over $1.7 million already paid to affiliates and 400,000+ customers. A published affiliate count of 2,500+ is absolute evidence of a large creator pool (compare Paula's Choice at 1,607 recorded high in an earlier batch), so creator_saturation is recorded as high. The brand's marketing is hype-heavy and its earnings claims are self-reported, which tempers the credibility score.

opportunity.title: Evil Goods Affiliate Program
opportunity.compensation_notes: 20% base commission on every sale (25% at $5K+ monthly sales, up to 30% in launch promos), lifetime commission on referred customers, 60-day cookie, monthly payouts at a $50 minimum, per the brand's own affiliate page. No earnings cap is stated, so the cap is unknown.
opportunity.description: Apply on Evil Goods' affiliate page, get a link or 15% follower code, and post tallow-skincare content; the brand says posts over 5,000 organic views can be sent in for paid ad support.

reasons: 20% base commission with lifetime customer commission, published on the brand's own page
Published affiliate contact email and 48-hour application review
2,500+ affiliates stated by the brand, so the program is already crowded
Self-reported earnings claims are hype-heavy and unverified, lowering credibility
